headline: Wet, windy storm today into Sunday, then drier and cooler by midweek.
summary: Storms are arriving from the Pacific. A dip in the high-altitude winds is crossing western Washington, and a stronger front is approaching just offshore. Together they bring rain and gusty winds through Sunday, strongest on the coast and in the eastern Strait, with flooding possible on the Skokomish River. Winds ease Sunday as the front moves east, and Monday brings scattered showers, mostly on the coast and in the hills. Drier weather returns Monday night into Tuesday. Later in the week, the storm track, or main path of storms across the Pacific, is expected to shift south of the region, bringing a cool, mostly dry end to the week. Forecasters are less sure about a light touch of rain in the south on Wednesday, and the dry outlook could still change.
